newsitem.title: GERMANY: Kloeckner to gain from reorganisation.
newsitem.headline: Kloeckner to gain from reorganisation.

text.p: German engineering group Kloeckner Werke AG on Thursday predicted its reorganisation and cost-cutting measures would lead to a small profit rise in the 1996/97 business year.

The company, which last year sold off one plastics unit and put another into a joint venture, expects group profit on ordinary activities of at least 50 million marks ($29.7 million), chief exeuctive Heinz-Ludwig Schmitz said.
This compares with 49.3 million marks in the year that ended on September 30.
Through the first five months of 1996/97, Kloeckner had group sales of 1.7 billion marks and 1.8 billion marks in new orders.
Both figures show increases from a year ago if organisational changes are factored in, Schmitz told the company's annual meeting in Duisburg.
"This should be a year of stabilisation," he said. "The results on ordinary activities should at least reach the level of last year, or about 50 million marks."
He said the slimmed-down firm expected about four billion marks in 1996/97 sales but gave no outlook on net profit, which was 700,000 marks last year after years of losses.
Schmitz also said the company wanted to resume dividend payments in three years -- after not providing payouts for the last 25 years.

The sale of Kloeckner's Kautex Group, a maker of plastic fuel tanks, and the consolidation of its Kalle plastic films business into a joint venture strengthened the group's revenue structure, he said.
The moves helped Kloeckner in cutting its debt to 950 million marks, down from 1.4 billion marks last year.
Group sales last year rose 2.5 percent to 4.5 billion marks, driven by auto supply sales, which rose 17 percent to 2.5 billion marks.
Bottling and packaging machinery sales fell 15 percent to 1.2 billion marks, hurt by consolidation in the brewing and beverage industries. Plastic film sales climbed 6 percent to 600 million marks.
Kloeckner's main challenge this year would be continuing cost-cutting in Germany, where high labour costs have hindered results.
"Above all, we at Kloeckner must now learn to make money in Germany," Schmitz said.
German sales fell four percent in 1995/96, while sales overseas rose 11 percent.
Kloeckner last year sold Kautex to Textron Inc. Kalle Hartfolien GmbH joined with a Hoeschst AG unit, Pentaplast GmbH, to form Kalle Pentaplast GmbH.
